correctness.rationale: All cyclic length-four line itineraries (consecutive labels distinct) are two-line alternations or have precisely one repeated line. Two-line alternation contracts to a vertex. Base repetition yields the four displayed nonvertex points, with branch margins 4h^4/((1+h^2)(h^2+2))>0 and -4h^2(h^4-h^2-1)/((1+h^2)(h^2+2)^2), so exactly 0<h<sqrt(phi) is admissible. Repeating either sloping side forces a base coordinate -(h^2-1)^2/(h^4+2h^2+5) <=0, requiring the wrong farthest line or a fixed tie. Unique affine fixed points for each itinerary prove an exhaustive global census for every h>0. The four-step multiplier (1+h^2)^-2 is strictly contracting. Independent exact-fraction nine-height enumeration and symbolic return calculations confirm critical formulas, not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The complete nonvertex least-period-four census for every h>0 has a genuine extension beyond published results: global uniqueness/exclusion of all alternative four-step itineraries and coverage of 0<h<=1.
